proposition: A cross-government strategy is needed to tackle health inequalities.
extract: This postcode lottery has led to entrenched health inequalities. Why osteoporosis requires urgent scrutiny and government-led action: Fracture prevention is hampered by (i) a lack of clinical leadership of osteoporosis within ICBs due to the condi tion not being owned by an y medical specialt y; (ii) under-r epresentation on medical training curricula; (iii) disincentives through QOF, and (iv) failure within the NHS to officially recognise osteoporosis as a long-term condition [xi] . Scrutiny is needed to understand what nationally mandated measures are needed to compel change across ICBs. Otherwise the current postcode lottery will remain entrenched and costs to the NHS, social care system and wider economy will spiral further as t he population ages.

extract: Many older people underestimate the importance of strength and conditioning, often associating physical decline with aging until a fall occurs. Public health campaigns showcasing active older adults can motivate and inform this population.

Patients need to be fully informed, offered choices and involved in their care. The need for flexible support to manage physical health needs is key to address reduced physical morbidity and reduced life expectancy. proposition: Mental health awareness training for school staff should be mandatory and integrated into Initial Teacher Training.
extract: Alongside ensuring there is a counsellor in every school, it is also important that school staff have an understanding of mental health issues and how to identify them . Schools are an excellent place to addre ss mental health concerns , but if the proper support and systems are not in place – for both children and teachers – then cases can be missed or not passed on for referral. It is , therefore , imperative that school staff are provided with adequat e training to help them spot any signs of distress, to feel confident in addressing the issue with the child (and if necessary the parent), and to provide them with the skills to advise families where to go to seek further help. We would recommend that teachers and t eaching assistants are offered courses in basic counselling skills , such as through Counselling MindEd, with regular refresher training, to provide them with these skills.
org: British Association for Counselling and Psychotherapy

proposition: Bureaucracy and administrative burdens in General Practice should be significantly reduced.
extract: Work with GPs to find out exactly what are the main causes and then find solutions to stop them. For example, CQC could be more supportive and less punitive, QoF pushes GPs into often little -evidenced large-scale work, a unified patient record would save huge amounts of time currently spent chasing information that is difficult to find. Institute the role of Medical Personal Assistants in general practice to help with administrative duties that are very time consuming and take GPs away from frontline patient care. Devolve responsibility for ‘Fit Notes’ away from GPs to other members of the healthcare team.
